title: Chinese open-MoE cohort crosses 15 percent OpenRouter share floor by Q3 2026
body: By Q3 2026 the Chinese frontier-open Mixture-of-Experts checkpoint cohort — Alibaba's Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B that landed on OpenRouter Thursday morning Pacific time plus the rolling-cadence successors lining up behind it (the Tsinghua KEG Lab MiniMax M2.7 235B port that already shipped through Unsloth v2026.5.26, DeepSeek-V4-Pro on the same OpenRouter board at the $1.10 input-token tier, and the Moonshot Kimi K3 plus Zhipu GLM-5 checkpoints publicly committed to a June rolling-cadence OpenRouter integration) crosses a 15 percent floor on OpenRouter's daily completion-volume share — the first time the Chinese frontier-open MoE cohort treats OpenRouter as a structurally-anchored distribution surface rather than a permissioned showcase. Thursday's first-six-hour routing telemetry on Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B already lifted the model to 4.7 percent of total OpenRouter completion volume across all listed models — the third-highest first-day share for any new model on the gateway behind only GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.7 — with median first-token latency holding at 0.16 seconds across the five-provider hosted pool (Alibaba Cloud Model Studio, Together AI, Fireworks AI, Hyperbolic, DeepInfra) and the default lowest-price-first routing policy landing roughly 73 percent of requests on Together AI plus Fireworks AI on the back of their FP8 quantization tier. Hugging Face's Thursday hosted-endpoint dashboard separately recorded the model crossing 1.04 million completion requests in the first eight hours of OpenRouter availability, and Simon Willison flagged the integration as the first Chinese frontier-open MoE checkpoint to land on OpenRouter inside its scheduled vendor-announced calendar window without slippage — the precondition that breaks the prior pattern of Chinese open checkpoints arriving on the gateway with weeks of slippage and price-floor-uncertainty that kept the routing-policy default skewed against them. The structural force is that once a Chinese frontier-open MoE checkpoint lands on on launch day across five hosted providers at a $0.45 per million input-token floor that undercuts DeepSeek-V4-Pro at $1.10 and Anthropic Claude Opus 4.7 at $7.50, the lowest-price-first routing policy pulls structural traffic onto the cohort automatically, the vLLM v0.11.5-rc1 expert-fused-router pass already serves the same checkpoint at 22,140 tokens per second on the Yotta Labs benchmark with 79.4 percent prefill cache hit-rate, and the Mistral Workflows five-vendor cross-orchestrator interop matrix that hit GA two weeks ahead of schedule normalizes calling these checkpoints from inside enterprise agent harnesses without per-vendor adapter friction. The most likely landing is that by Q3 2026 OpenRouter's daily completion-volume share for the Chinese frontier-open MoE cohort crosses 15 percent on the rolling seven-day median — driven by Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B holding the high single digits plus at least two of the three June-cohort integrations (DeepSeek, Moonshot, Zhipu) clearing 2 percent each — with at least one US-headquartered hyperscaler-managed inference tier publishing a public BYO-checkpoint configuration page citing the OpenRouter price-floor cohort as the reference comparand. Bear case is a US Commerce Department BIS export-control adjustment that bars one of the five hosted providers from continuing to serve the cohort inside the Q3 window, capping share at 9 to 11 percent; absent that intervention, Q3 2026 lands the Chinese frontier-open MoE cohort at a structural 15 percent OpenRouter share floor.

reasoning.given: Five hosted providers + $0.45/Mtoken floor + vLLM v0.11.5-rc1 serving it at 22140 tok/s.
reasoning.so_that: Lowest-price-first routing default pulls structural traffic onto the Chinese frontier-open MoE cohort.
reasoning.landing: By Q3 2026; cohort crosses 15 percent rolling-7d share on OpenRouter.
reasoning.plain_language: Chinese open AI models are getting cheap and fast on the big AI marketplace, so they will soon take a steady share of traffic.

summary: Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B launched on OpenRouter Thursday across five hosted providers at a $0.45 input-token floor, hitting 4.7 percent first-day share and 1.04M requests in 8 hours. By Q3 2026 the Chinese frontier-open MoE cohort crosses a 15 percent OpenRouter daily completion-volume share floor.
